comparator.name: History (Geschiedenis)
comparator.sourceNotes: Dutch Geschiedenis, Algemeen direction, 2026–27 adopted OER26May2026, revised PDF filename27August2026. Physical pages22–23 inspected: Year1 four9ECsurveys and four6ECskills/philosophy units=60; Year2 compulsory48 plus first-listed period1 Capitalism and Inequality6 and period2 Latin America in Modern History6=60; Year3 open30 + compulsory Culture/Religion/Knowledge500–1800research9 + exactly one Global research seminar9 + colloquium3 + thesis9=60. The first listed Global/Political seminar is selected independently of UCR fit; the alternative Global/Economic/Social seminar is not stacked. Current annual317focuses Low Countries lay devotion1350–1800, manuscripts/oldprints and digital/archival methods. Current318focuses political photography from nineteenth century onwards; it is not an unrestricted global-history seminar. Future themes/offerings can change. OER9.1 Year3seminars require allYear1; thesis and colloquium require allYear1/2. Annualcolloquium requires a signed thesis agreement and actual topic/supervisor contact by period4; thesis grade is withheld until colloquium satisfactorily completed. Thesis is supervised individual literature-based historical research, optionally primary sources. Language diagnostic/refresher gates AcVa grade. BSA42first-yearEC plus AcVa and language test. Practicals/tutorials80percent; annualOralHistory attendance compulsory, research317paper>=6. Open30 requires boardconsent, individual package>=12EClevel300, with eligible University/faculty minor consent exceptions and compulsory overlap replacement approval. Placement12+electives18 or abroad30 occupies same allowance. Zero-credit Dutch test not added to180; English-route language/skills rules not substituted.

alternatives.concept: A historical core in modern change, gender, empire, war and Indigenous histories leads into cultural heritage, memory and interpretation through art, archaeology, life-writing, historiography and media. The final historical research seminar examines primary sources about Walcheren in 1809. These companion fields do not reproduce VU specialist historical coverage or compulsory individual thesis.

alternatives.concept: Historical investigation of empire, warfare and American gender/Indigenous histories leads into rights, political institutions, conflict and social inclusion. alternatives.concept: The same historical core and source-critical research progression are combined with economic theory, statistical inference and social theory to investigate mechanisms of economic and political change. Economic models and data analysis are complementary tools, not substitutes for economic history or VU History by Numbers. The final historical research is the Walcheren 1809 source project; no historical dataset application in Econometrics is guaranteed.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The Dutch Geschiedenis target uses its general Algemeen graduation direction, the broadest route, rather than a specialized direction or the distinct English History and International Studies trajectory. Second-year choices use the first listed 6-EC course in each period; the third-year extra research seminar uses the first listed alternative. No selection is based on UCR fit.

progressionAssessment.rationale: All 24-course, 180-EC, level-300, PPD, exact semester-availability and hard-prerequisite checks passed. Foundational historical and social inquiry precedes final historical research; contemporary courses are explicitly related applications, not substitutes for period-specific historical modules. The six core History courses run in all alternatives. The research seminar is placed last; course-description-only evidence is identified where the enriched workbook has no outline.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Retain three qualified, substantively distinct responses after challenging each from actual content, contribution and weight. Each contains all six available History courses / 45 EC: modern history, American gender history with interviews, empire, warfare, Native American social/cultural history, and a final archival/primary-source research paper on Walcheren 1809. This is sustained historical object/method/progression, not merely a coherent unrelated programme or a generic interest in society. Cultural heritage/public memory adds art/archaeology, historiography, life-writing and historical media; political conflict/social inclusion adds institutions, rights, international relations and sociological enquiry; political economy adds five economic theory/inference courses plus social theory to study mechanisms of historical change. These companions have distinct taught objects/methods and change substantial course weight, not just labels. Their relevance does not make economics, statistics, sociology or contemporary politics into economic/migration history. No UCR composition reproduces VU broader medieval/early-modern and Netherlands sequences, Holocaust-centred genocide historiography, digital-history training, Low Countries devotion research, specialist photography seminar or individual History thesis. Numerical overlap is a feasibility/traceability check, not the comparability argument. Three pass on this basis; no fourth omnibus or generic-method alternative is justified. Two additional candidate directions are explicitly rejected: the illustrative crime-history question (row 4568) does not establish specialist Holocaust/genocide progression in the available UCR courses; migration history (row 4574) has limited support through historical gender/Indigenous inquiry and contemporary inclusion, but lacks a distinct specialist migration-history composition. Their formal registry generator roles remain accounted for through rejected candidates, without authorising another included programme.

notes.text: These are qualified historical responses with cultural, political or economic companions. VU additionally requires specialist medieval/early-modern, Netherlands, Holocaust/genocide, digital-history and regional research work, a current photography-based global seminar and a compulsory individual thesis. UCR statistics and economics do not replace those units; the UCR History Research Seminar concerns Walcheren 1809. Current annual topics and future offerings can change.

audience.programmeDescription: VU History studies Europe and the wider world from antiquity to the present. Students learn to evaluate historical evidence, develop arguments and conduct research through source-based seminars and an individual thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: Three qualified UCR alternatives retain a historical core and a final primary-source research project. They develop cultural heritage and memory, political conflict and social inclusion, or political economy as distinct companion fields. They do not reproduce VU specialist period, regional and digital-history training or its compulsory individual thesis.

curriculum.limitation: The 180 EC illustration includes two selected Year-2 choices, 30 EC open study, a compulsory 9 EC culture/religion research unit, one selected 9 EC global research seminar, a 3 EC colloquium and a 9 EC thesis. The current selected global seminar studies political photography. Year-3 seminars require all Year 1; thesis and colloquium require all Years 1 and 2. Language testing, attendance, elective-level and approval rules apply; research themes and offerings can change.
